messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Error: cannot find Exiftool
parts:
Dear John and Melissa,
an alternative way to test if R can find exiftool is to run:

system("exiftool")

If R can find exiftool, you should see the exiftool documentation in your console (basically, a lot of text).

Regarding Johns qustion, exiftool is in "C:/Windows/Exiftool/exiftool.exe" ? If so, try

exiftool_dir<-"C:/Windows/Exiftool"      
exiftoolPath(exiftoolDir = exiftool_dir)

Argument exiftoolDir is meant to point to the directory containing exiftool.exe, not the file itself.
Alternatively, put the exiftool file in "C:/Windows", i.e. "C:/Windows/exiftool.exe"

Melissa, you could try the same to see if it helps.
Best,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: Error: cannot find Exiftool
parts:
Thanks for the screenshot. I believe the problem is Windows hiding file extensions of known files. It is the default, but can cause problems and is unsafe too.

Follow the instructions here to show file extensions of known file types (the box highlighted in red at the bottom):
https://www.file-extensions.org/article/show-and-hide-file-extensions-in-windows-10

Then I believe you'll see that because of this behaviour of Windows, you accidentally renamed the file to 

exiftool.exe.exe

If so, rename to exiftool.exe and you should be good.
Jürgen

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Error: cannot find Exiftool
parts:
Hi Megan,
error 127 means that the system call cannot find exiftool in the PATH variables (that's where it looks for a executable files).
So you need to make sure that R / your system has the folder containing exiftool.exe in its PATH variables. 
You can check which directories are in PATH via:
Sys.getenv("PATH")

The easiest way to add a folder to PATH from within R is via camtrapR's addToPath() function (previously called exiftoolPath):
addToPath("C:/PATH/TO/EXIFTOOL")

Afterwards the system should be able to find exiftool.exe in the folder C:/PATH/TO/EXIFTOOL

Please also see the section "ExifTool for Windows" in vignette 1:
https://jniedballa.github.io/camtrapR/articles/camtrapr1.html
(note, I didn't update the vignette and it still contains the old function name exiftoolPath() instead of addToPath())

Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Error: cannot find Exiftool
parts:
Hello, 
the vignette 1 of camtrapR describes the manual installation process, but since you mentioned the install_exiftool function from the exiftoolr package let's go with that.
 
library(exiftoolr)
install_exiftool()
exif_version()  # prints "13.30" and confirms the installation was successful

Now find the location of exiftool:
> configure_exiftoolr()
Trying perl command: "" --version
Trying perl command: "perl" --version
Trying perl command: "C:\Perl64\bin\perl" --version
Trying perl command: "C:\Perl\bin\perl" --version
Trying perl command: "C:\Strawberry\perl\bin\perl" --version
Trying exiftool command: "C:\Users\USERNAME\AppData\Roaming/R/data/R/exiftoolr/win_exe/exiftool.exe" -ver
ExifTool found at: "C:\Users\USERNAME\AppData\Roaming/R/data/R/exiftoolr/win_exe/exiftool.exe"    

See the last line, that's the install location. exiftoolr puts the exiftool.exe in it's own little personal folder. Now we need to pass that to addToPath().
Be careful to:
  • set the USERNAME
  • not include the .exe file
  • use only forward slashes

addToPath("C:/Users/USERNAME/AppData/Roaming/R/data/R/exiftoolr/win_exe")

Now R can find exiftool:

> Sys.which("exiftool")
                                                                            exiftool
"C:\\Users\\USERNA~1\\AppData\\Roaming\\R\\data\\R\\EXIFTO~1\\win_exe\\exiftool.exe" 

I just tried this, it works. When you start a new R session you only need to call one command:

addToPath("C:/Users/USERNAME/AppData/Roaming/R/data/R/exiftoolr/win_exe")

with the modified user name. Then all camtrapR function which rely on exiftool should work like normal.

Thank you for bringing this up, it's good to have another, potentially easier, way to install exiftool.

Let me know if it still doesn't work. 
Jürgen

Thanks for the screenshot. I believe the problem is Windows hiding file extensions of known files. It is the default, but can cause problems and is unsafe too.

Follow the instructions here to show file extensions of known file types (the box highlighted in red at the bottom):
https://www.file-extensions.org/article/show-and-hide-file-extensions-in-windows-10

Then I believe you'll see that because of this behaviour of Windows, you accidentally renamed the file to 

exiftool.exe.exe

If so, rename to exiftool.exe and you should be good.
